our_view.thesis_status: Post-restructuring operating trends are improving off the trough: June 2026 marks three straight months of rising revenue and Reported EBITDA, weak sites down to 8 (from a peak of 9), and agency-labor dependence down to 10.0% of revenue (from a Q4 2025 peak of 17.6%) -- consistent with pillars 1 and 4 holding and pillar 2 showing real, if partial, progress (graded 'pressured' rather than 'intact' since 8 of 15 sites remain unprofitable and revenue is still ~17% below the approved budget and well below the pre-2025 run-rate). Pillar 3 (covenant reinstatement) is graded 'pressured': the informational FCCR has WORSENED every quarter since the restructuring closed (1.05x at 2025-Q4 -> 0.67x at 2026-Q1 -> 0.37x at 2026-Q2), purely on trailing-twelve-month math still absorbing the 2025 collapse -- it should mechanically improve through year-end as those months roll off, but that has not yet been demonstrated. The September 30, 2026 FCCR reinstatement-readiness milestone (Stabilization Milestone M4, PENDING) is the key near-term test, due in two weeks from this review. Restructuring accounting (TDR framework, instrument-level test, goodwill interim reassessment) remains PROVISIONAL nearly six months after close, which is itself worth escalating if it persists much longer.
our_view.what_would_change_our_mind: A fourth consecutive month of EBITDA/revenue improvement with weak-site count at or below 8 and agency-labor % holding near or below 10% would support upgrading trajectory further and reconsidering watchlist status. Conversely, a reversal of June's improvement, a missed or unfavorable September 30 FCCR reinstatement-readiness milestone, or the provisional restructuring/goodwill accounting resolving unfavorably (a larger loss, higher carrying debt, or an additional impairment) would move this back toward 'deteriorating' and keep or deepen the watchlist flag.

business._archetype_note: JUDGMENT CALL: none of the three named archetypes is a clean fit for a multi-site fee-for-service healthcare operator. 'consumer-inventory' clearly does not fit (no inventory, not consumer/D2C). 'asset-heavy-industrial' does not fit either -- there is no order book/backlog and collateral recovery here is receivables-led, not equipment-led. 'services-project' is the closer of the two remaining options: payroll IS the burn floor (Labor tab), DSO/AR-claims collection is the key working-capital swing factor, and collateral recovery is genuinely receivables-led -- but its 'backlog/bookings/contract concentration' framing is BPO/agency-specific and doesn't describe payer-claims/visit-volume economics. Flagging for the analyst to confirm or to propose a dedicated healthcare-services archetype in monthly-monitor references/archetypes.md.
business.business_one_liner: Operates a 15-site, 5-region outpatient healthcare-services platform, billing a diversified payer mix (Medicare, Commercial, Medicaid, Workers' Compensation, Self-Pay) for patient visits and clinical procedures.

Asteron Care Holdings, Inc. is named only as the corporate guarantor/parent, not identified as the sponsor. Flagged for analyst confirmation of the sponsor's identity.

business_profile.description: Asteron Care Partners operates a multi-site, multi-region outpatient healthcare-services platform (15 clinical sites across five regional operating subsidiaries -- Southeast, Mid-Atlantic, Northeast, Great Lakes, and Central Operations, LLC), billing commercial and government payers on a fee-for-service basis for patient visits and clinical procedures. The company underwent a debt-for-equity restructuring in March 2026 after 2025 volume and cost pressure eroded coverage.

facility.instrument: Senior secured term loan (reinstated exit term debt + new-money term debt, single first-priority lien class)
facility.draw_structure: single advance at restructuring close (no revolver or delayed-draw commitment) -- $44,000,000 reinstated debt (exchanged from predecessor/legacy debt) + $7,000,000 new-money term debt, funded 2026-03-31
facility.interest_rate: Fixed cash interest: 11.50% through March 2026, stepping down to 10.00% from April 2026 onward; no floating index disclosed. Monthly principal amortization stepped down from 0.70%/month (Predecessor/Legacy) to 0.10%/month beginning April 2026. No PIK disclosed.
facility.oid: None disclosed. Debt issuance costs of $1,200,000 were capitalized as a deferred financing asset at close (successor gross debt $51,000,000 vs. provisional successor carrying debt $49,800,000 per the Predecessor Close/Successor Opening workpaper; carrying debt per the June 2026 package is $49,707,152.95 after 3 months' amortization). Debt/equity accounting for the exchange itself (TDR framework, instrument-level 10% modification test) is explicitly PROVISIONAL pending workpapers not yet concluded.

fees.Closing-date fees: Debt issuance costs of $1,200,000 and restructuring advisory fees of $1,800,000 per the executed Sources & Uses (Restructuring Closing Materials); the executed Fee Letter (effective 2026-03-31) references 'debt issuance and administrative fees per the executed closing statement' but does not itemize dollar amounts in the available text -- sourced instead from the Sources & Uses workbook.
fees.Prior bridge fee: $140,000 upfront fee on the $7,000,000 Exit Amendment bridge facility (Dec 2025), superseded/rolled into the March 2026 exit capitalization; recorded as a below-EBITDA expense in the December 2025 Income Statement.

facility.equity_kicker: None disclosed as a lender warrant/kicker. The restructuring itself converted $16,910,820.62 of predecessor debt into Series A preferred equity held by former debtholders (debt-for-equity exchange, not a lender warrant), alongside $8,000,000 of new common equity from the (unnamed) sponsor.
facility.security: First-priority blanket lien on substantially all assets of the borrower and guarantors (accounts, chattel paper, deposit accounts, equipment, fixtures, general intangibles, instruments, inventory, books/records, proceeds) per the executed Guaranty and Security Agreement (effective 2026-03-31); controlled/concentration deposit accounts; guarantees from Asteron Care Holdings, Inc. and the five regional operating subsidiaries.

credit_thesis.pillar: Reduced funded debt ($51.0M vs. $60.9M pre-restructuring) and reduced monthly amortization (0.10% vs. 0.70% of principal), combined with $8.0M of new sponsor equity and $12.0M of retained successor liquidity, give the company enough runway to execute the stabilization plan without a near-term liquidity event.
credit_thesis.monitored_by: Cash balance vs. the $10.0M minimum-liquidity control; monthly debt service (Debt and Equity tab)

credit_thesis.pillar: Site-level and labor remediation (agency-vendor rate-card reset, 8-site remediation plans) restores site profitability and reduces agency-labor dependence enough to return Reported EBITDA to a run-rate that could support FCCR reinstatement by the September 30, 2026 milestone.
credit_thesis.monitored_by: Weak-site count; agency/contract-labor % of revenue; Reported EBITDA trend (Income Statement / Site Operations support)

credit_thesis.pillar: The legacy 1.2000x FCCR covenant, though contractually SUSPENDED through December 31, 2026, remains informationally tracked every period so the lender can assess reinstatement readiness rather than being blind to the credit's true trajectory.
credit_thesis.monitored_by: Informational TTM FCCR vs. 1.2000x (Covenant Calculation / Compliance Certificate)

credit_thesis.pillar: The first-priority blanket collateral package (cash, receivables, PP&E, general intangibles) continues to support recovery even though it is not relied upon as the primary source of repayment.
credit_thesis.monitored_by: Collateral coverage vs. funded debt (Collateral metrics box)

business._credit_thesis_note: The one-page Restructuring IC Memo does not itself enumerate discrete thesis 'pillars' -- these four were constructed by monitor-setup from the memo's stated Decision/rationale and the A&R Agreement's own stabilization mechanics (minimum liquidity, weekly reporting, named milestones), not copied from an explicit pillar list. transcription_notes: min_liquidity's certified actual ($18,817,443.79) is transcribed from the companion 2026-Q2 PM Update.pdf 'LIQUIDITY' line, not from Compliance Certificate.pdf itself -- this quarter's compliance certificate text states only the FCCR calculation and disposition, with no liquidity figure printed on it. Both documents sit in the same Portfolio Monitoring/2026-Q2 folder and are read together as the quarter's compliance-certificate/covenant-calculation exhibit per covenant-spec.json's min_liquidity cert_ref. The engine attaches one upstream document address to every value transcribed into this file (its top-level 'source' field, set here to Compliance Certificate.pdf), so the archived source_ref for the liquidity row's certified side will display the Compliance Certificate.pdf address even though the number itself came from PM Update.pdf in the same folder -- the quote field above carries the correct citation regardless.

performance.methodology: Company-prepared/unaudited monthly financials model (read via monitor_lib). EBITDA is the model's single pinned bridge row. Normalized metrics strip config.comparability_items. Ratios are spot on latest-month flows; leverage/coverage are TTM within the current same-basis segment when >=12 such months exist. Standouts, drift, trend and the MoM bridge are objective/mechanical and confined to same-basis segments; the line read covers EVERY IS/BS leaf with rule-based flags (no statistical gating); narrative interpretation is left to synthesis.

ap-ar-aging.note: No AR/AP aging-summary export exists for this borrower in a shape ap_ar_aging.py's parser can read. The only monthly AR/AP file is 'source:Asteron Care Partners/Successor Reporting/2026/06/ar-ap-support.xlsx' (and its May-2026 prior-month counterpart at 'source:Asteron Care Partners/Successor Reporting/Archive/2026-05/ar-ap-support.xlsx'), which carries two sheets -- 'AR Claims' (229 rows) and 'AP Invoices' (53 rows) -- each a CLAIM/INVOICE-LEVEL transaction list (one row per claim/invoice: Claim/Invoice #, Payer class/Vendor, Entity/Category, date, Original, Balance, Disputed, a single 'Bucket' label per row, Status) with NO 'Total' column and no grand-total row. This does not match any shape the engine's parser handles per module-ap-ar-aging.md's 'Export shapes the parser handles' (a customer/vendor-per-row grid with per-bucket DOLLAR columns and a Total column/row). Running ap_ar_aging.py directly against the file confirms this: it self-skips with 'ValueError: could not locate aging header row in ar-ap-support.xlsx'. Checked the rest of the deal folder for a dedicated bucketed aging export: 'Portfolio Monitoring' (2025-Q1 through 2026-Q2) holds only quarterly Compliance Certificate / Covenant Calculation (FCCR) / PM Update files, and Successor Reporting's monthly.xlsx carries only Status/Income Statement/Balance Sheet/Cash Flow/Debt and Equity/Budget versus Actual/Trial Balance/Covenant tabs -- no aging tab or export exists anywhere else for this borrower, and every archived month back to 2024-09 carries the same claim/invoice-level 'ar-ap-support.xlsx' shape (checked 2026-05 explicitly). The underlying transaction data is otherwise sound and reconciles: summing the June-2026 'Balance' column gives AR $20,896,429.14 and AP $5,433,050.66, tying EXACTLY to the June-2026 Balance Sheet Accounts receivable / Accounts payable rows in the model (both on model.scale=1, whole dollars -- confirmed against the model workbook's Balance Sheet tab -- so aging.amount_scale=1 as configured in borrower-config is correct and there is no unit mismatch to flag). The gap is purely an export SHAPE the shared engine's parser does not read, not missing or bad data. Reshaping the 282 claim/invoice rows into the counterparty x bucket grid the parser expects would mean this worker computing the module's own bucket/concentration/DSO-DPO arithmetic outside the audited, reproducible engine, which is out of scope for a single-run fix; the parser needs a durable claim/invoice-level (transaction-level) input mode -- group by payer class (AR) / vendor (AP), sum Balance within each row's own Bucket label -- added to ap_ar_aging.py as a follow-on engineering task before this module can run for Asteron in any period.
